acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT.
1. THE SHAPE, AND WHY. ONE MERGED MONTH DOCUMENT at the same canonical key -- not per-partner keys and not a manifest. The axis is WHO READS THIS AND WHAT THEY SEE: the reader is a person opening ONE file to decide whether Opal goes outside for data, so the property 'which partners does this cover' has to live in the STORED DOCUMENT. Per-partner keys are the more obvious fix and are worse on that axis: they make each file correct while leaving a partner that never wrote INVISIBLE to anyone who does not already know the partner set -- which is precisely the failure being repaired, moved from an overwrite to an absence. A manifest has the same defect one level up (a manifest that omits a partner reads as complete). So the document now carries `partners_covered`, derived from its own merged content, and `ask_scope`.
2. AND THE MERGE'S OWN FAILURE MODE IS DECLARED, NOT HIDDEN. A merge has exactly one input: the read of what is already at the key. If that read is unavailable, a naive merge silently degrades to the original overwrite -- the same artifact, the same invisibility. So `_read_prior_asks` distinguishes an absent CAPABILITY from an absent OBJECT: a client with no get_object returns readable=False and the document says `ask_scope: 'partner-only (prior asks UNREADABLE -- this file may omit other partners)'`, while a get_object that merely raises is read as the ordinary first-partner absence and stays month-complete. A reader is never handed a file that looks complete and is not.
3. WHAT THE SERVED 2026-09 ARTIFACT OMITS, with counts and vintage -- this is the artifact a person would have authorised on. s3://opal-data-etfs/platinum/reports/2026-09/coverage_egress_ask.json, 1017 bytes, LastModified 2026-09-10T01:20:20Z (s3api head-object, UTC), written by EG-s-15's real September run. It names 1 ask, partner ['cottonwood'], date 2026-09-09. The month's own coverage_unresolved.json (same prefix, same run) carries 2 outstanding days across ['49financial','cottonwood']. So the served ask names 1 OF 2 outstanding days and OMITS ('49financial','2026-09-09') entirely, and its top-level keys are ['month','generated_at','asks','authorization'] -- there is no field in it from which a reader could learn that a second partner existed. A person authorising on it would have approved half of what was outstanding while believing they had seen all of it.
4. A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER ROW. W1-S27 (filed by me on EG-s-15) reported this same 1-of-2 shortfall correctly as an OBSERVATION but speculated the cause was an unmapped provider for 49financial. That speculation was WRONG and this cell's read disproves it: remediate.py's _PROVIDER_BY_PARTNER maps 49financial -> 'Schwab' explicitly. The cause is the partner-less key and the per-partner call, not the provider map. The row hedged the cause as 'likely', which is why it was a hypothesis and not a finding, but a reader chasing the provider map would have found nothing wrong there.
5. CONSUMERS OF THE KEY, CENSUSED WITH A DENOMINATOR RATHER THAN RECALLED. comp-find 'coverage_egress_ask' over the repo corpus: 124 hits across 29716 files scanned, banded SURFACED=36 CONFIG=8 TEST=33 DOC=47. Outside remediate.py itself and the test files, exactly ONE first-party consumer reads the key: infra/aws/lambda/etfs-reports-orchestrator/lambda_function.py, which fetches it in _read_coverage_artifacts (:254, the ('coverage_egress_ask.json','ask') pair) and renders it in _build_terminal_email. Its consumption was READ, not recalled: :292 `if ask and ask.get("asks")`, :296 `for a in ask["asks"]` with per-entry `.get('date'/'partner'/'provider'/'class'/'reason')`, and :300 `ask.get('authorization')`. IT IS NOT BROKEN BY THIS SHAPE CHANGE: every key it touches is unchanged, the per-entry shape is unchanged, and the two new top-level keys are additive; the only difference it sees is that `asks` is now COMPLETE, which makes the terminal email more complete rather than less. NOTE ON LANE: that file is 0.9.0_WK_ETFS_GUARDRAIL~4's live surface for EG-s-21 and was READ ONLY -- not edited, not staged, not touched.
6. WHAT THIS CHANGE DOES NOT REPAIR. (i) IT DOES NOT FIX THE SERVED ARTIFACT. The 2026-09 ask still omits 49financial's day and this cell writes no served key; the artifact only becomes complete when a ladder runs again against DEPLOYED bytes that carry this change. (ii) IT IS NOT DEPLOYED: DEPLOYED != BUILT, deployed sha256 3c3ce6c5cfcce654... (11011 B, equal to the pre-change blob) vs built 25ff4dbed4af6545... (15011 B), so every future run today still overwrites one partner's ask with the next; the deploy is a separate act with a separate owner. (iii) It does not repair the rung-1/rung-2 ladder, which was not this cell's subject and is untouched. (iv) It does not make a partner that NEVER RUNS AT ALL appear in the document -- no per-partner function can know a set it was never given -- but such a partner is now visibly absent from `partners_covered` instead of invisibly absent from a document with no coverage field, which is the property the bar asked for. (v) It does not touch inflection's producer or any egress authorization; ruling card 4's PER-USE line is unchanged and stands for nobody.
